Get talking — four steps4
1
Switch onTurn the volume knob clockwise until it clicks. The screen shows your zone and channel.
2
Pick the channelTurn the selector to the K2SHUT26 channel for your crew — the list is right above.
3
Listen firstCheck nobody is already talking. Only one person transmits at a time.
4
Press and talkHold PTT, wait a second, then speak 2.5–5 cm from your mouth. Release to listen.
Before each shift5
  • Charged — battery healthy, or swap it
  • Antenna hand-tight and undamaged
  • Right channel for your crew and task
  • Radio check — call another set, confirm you are heard
  • Faulty? Tag it, quarantine it, write it up
What the light means3
Solid redTransmitting — you are talking
Blinking greenReceiving a call, or powering up
Blinking yellowScanning, or no channel activity
Keep every call as short as you can. All radios are signed out and signed back in, returned clean and undamaged, and any fault reported straight away.
CIS-GDE-001 · Rev 2.0 · Motorola MOTOTRBO DP4801e
Honeywell BW Flex4
Check it. Wear it.
Trust it. Live it.
No pass = no issue. A damaged, overdue or failed monitor does not leave the store.
Before use5
1
Check the monitorNo damage. Sensor openings clean and clear. Battery charged. No warning, fault, calibration-due or bump-due message.
2
Turn it on in fresh airPress and hold the grey front button for 4 seconds.
3
Let the start-up checks finishConfirm the screen, lights, sound and vibration all work.
4
Wear it correctlyClip it on your chest or collar. Keep it uncovered and the sensor openings clear.
5
If it alarmsStop work. Leave the area and move somewhere safe. Warn others. Report it and follow the site emergency procedure. Never silence an alarm and keep working.
Typical clean-air readings4
LEL0
O₂20.9
H₂S0
CO0
Alarm = action4
High alarmLeave the area immediately. Move to fresh air. Follow the emergency procedure.
Low alarmBe aware. Assess the situation. Leave the area if required.
STEL / TWA alarmTake action. Follow site procedures. Monitor your exposure.
Fault warningThe monitor is not working properly. Tag it out. Do not use it. Report it.
Only ever zero the monitor in known fresh air — never in a hazardous area. Bump test before use each day: no bump, no use. To turn it off, move somewhere safe and hold the front button for about 4 seconds until the countdown finishes.
Unsure about anything? Stop and ask. Safety is in our control — everyone, everywhere, every day.
Quick reference only. The stamp on the gear, the tag on the sling, the printed card at the counter and the manufacturer's procedure always win. If this page and the job's procedure disagree, the procedure is right.
Socket drive sizes
Check the square drive on the tool or the socket. 1/2" is the most common.
DRIVESIZEWHAT IT IS FORTYPICAL SOCKETS
1/4"6.35 mmSmallest drive — precision work
Electrical, instrument, small engine, electronics		4 – 14 mm
3/8"9.53 mmGeneral purpose workshop
General maintenance, automotive, light industrial		8 – 24 mm
1/2"12.7 mmHeavy duty — most applications
Shutdowns, construction, mining, industrial maintenance		10 – 36 mm
3/4"19.05 mmVery heavy duty — high torque
Structural, flange work, heavy equipment, large bolts		10 – 36 mm
1"25.4 mmExtreme heavy duty — maximum torque
Mining, excavators, draglines, large industrial equipment		46 – 80 mm+
How to tell the drive size
1 · Look insideCheck the square hole in the socket. That is the drive size.
2 · Check the anvilLook at the square on the impact gun or ratchet.
3 · Look for markingsMost sockets and tools are stamped with the drive size.
4 · Compare the sizeThe bigger the square, the bigger the drive.
Impact vs chrome
Getting this wrong is how sockets shatter.
IMPACT socket (black)Stronger steel, thicker walls, black phosphate.
Use with impact guns only.
CHROME socket (silver)Chrome vanadium, thinner walls, chrome plated.
Hand tools (ratchet) only — never on a rattle gun.
Socket types
TYPEWHAT IT IS FOR
Standard (shallow)Most common, general use
DeepFor long bolts and studs
6 pointBetter grip on fasteners
12 pointMore contact with the fastener
Impact (black)Impact guns only

CombinationOpen end and ring end. The all-rounder.

Flogging spannerUsed with a hammer — extra tightening or loosening.
AdjustableAdjustable jaw. When the exact size is unknown.
Offset ringOffset for clearance over obstructions.

Bolting sequences
Recommended general patterns — numbers opposite each other, working out from the centre. The manufacturer's procedure wins.
4 BOLT
6 BOLT
8 BOLT
10 BOLT
12 BOLT
16 BOLT
18 BOLT
20 BOLT
Bolting guidelines
AlwaysFollow the manufacturer's specific bolting procedure when provided.
In stagesTighten in stages — typically 30%, 60%, then 100% of final torque.
Criss-crossWork in a criss-cross pattern from the centre outward.
Clean and lubricatedMating surfaces clean, threads lubricated as specified.
Re-checkRe-check torque if the procedure requires it.

Before you pick it up
Wear the glassesEvery time, no exceptions.
Right tool for the jobA flogging spanner is not a hammer handle and a chrome socket is not an impact socket.
Impact sockets on impact gunsBlack on the rattle gun. Silver on the ratchet.
Never exceed the ratingDo not exceed the tool's or the fastener's torque rating.
